plans.headline: Carve foam stamps and print your own art

main.why: At Brentwood Park, artist Adam Cooley helps kids cut simple shapes and make their own foam stamps. Your child makes a print to take home.
tips: Wear play clothes that can get messy.
Bring a snack and water for a break between prints.
Let your child pick the shapes, and say the last print is the one to take home.

alternatives.why: Beech Bluff Explorers at 10:00 am is a hunt for animal signs. A family needs to sign up first. Then the playground at Beech Bluff County Park.
tips: Sign up ahead and meet at the Canopy Room.
Ask your child to be a detective and guess who was here.
Save the playground until the hunt is done.

alternatives.why: Muddy Boots at 9:00 am starts with a nature book, then a walk to find nature at the park. A family needs to sign up first. Then Twin Lakes Park.
tips: Sign up ahead and wear boots that can get dirty.
Bring a small bag for leaves and acorns.

alternatives.why: Family Storytime at Eva Perry Regional Library at 10:30 am has books, rhymes and movement. Then a run at Apex Community Park.
tips: Pick up a ticket at the Youth Services desk.
Bring a snack for the playground.

alternatives.why: Learn to Ride a Bike at Gipson Play Plaza runs from 2:00 to 4:00 pm for kids and families. Your child can try at a gentle pace.
tips: Bring your child's bike and a helmet if you have them.
Take water breaks and cheer for every wobble.

timeline.title: Wind down
timeline.detail: A couple of books to settle.

plans.headline: Stroll by the lake, then play on the playground

main.why: Walk the lakeside greenway and look at the water, then spend time on the playground. There is a picnic shelter for a snack before home.
tips: Bring a snack to eat at the picnic shelter.
Make a game of finding the biggest puddle, the flattest rock and the tallest tree.
Say the playground is the last stop so leaving feels planned.

alternatives.why: Learn to Ride a Bike at Gipson Play Plaza runs from 2:00 to 4:00 pm for kids and families. This is an afternoon outing after quiet time.
tips: Bring your child's bike and a helmet if you have them.
Take water breaks and cheer for every wobble.

plans.headline: Wander a garden, then greenway and playground

main.why: Walk the greenway, explore the garden and spend a long stretch on the playground. A picnic shelter gives you a place for a snack.
tips: Bring a snack and eat at the picnic shelter halfway through.
Give your child a job: find three kinds of leaves and one smooth stone.
Pick the last stop early so leaving feels like part of the plan.
